report: Today the only trade closed us out. Infineon opened weak after a premarket quote of 47.00, down almost five percent, as the AI chip selloff spread from Asia. Our stop was at about 46.82. The system sold all 6 shares at 09:05 UTC at 46.701, a little below the stop level, so the market gapped through it. Commission was 2.50 euros. The trader made no new decisions and placed no orders. The trade lost 30.16 euros net, minus 9.88 percent, against a planned stop of about minus 8 percent. Entry was 50.90 on November 10. It was held 10 days and was due to exit on November 24. The day result was minus 18.36 euros, or minus 0.92 percent. Equity is 1,969.83 euros, all cash, down 1.51 percent in total. There are no open positions and no pending orders. Reconcile is consistent. One warning: a shadow call, Worldline down 5 days, was rejected. On luck versus skill: the Infineon news was real and strong. But a sector-wide selloff overrode the news. One losing trade says almost nothing about the method. The useful lesson is about mechanics. A stop can fill below its level on a gap open, so expect real losses to be larger than the stop distance.
questions: The stop filled at 46.701 against a level of about 46.82, and the loss was -9.88% against a planned -8%. Should position sizing assume extra loss beyond the stop on gap opens, and how much?

Infineon had a strong company-specific catalyst but fell with the whole AI chip sector. Should the trader check sector or market stress, such as VIX near 28 or a chip selloff, before buying on company news?
The Worldline down-5-day shadow call was rejected. Why was it rejected, and is the rejection rule doing what we want for short calls on names we will not trade?

lessons.rule: Hypothesis: a stop can fill below its level when the stock gaps at the open, so the real loss can exceed the planned stop distance; size positions for that.
lessons.evidence: IFX.DE 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-20: stop about 46.82 (-8%), filled 46.701 at 09:05 UTC, net -9.88%. One case only.
